task: Summarize this incident for a status page in at most three sentences: a deploy at 14:05 doubled the database load, requests were slow for 20 minutes, the deploy was rolled back at 14:25, and load returned to normal.
rubric: The summary says that requests were slow for about twenty minutes.
It names the deploy as the cause and the rollback as the fix.
It says that things are back to normal.
It runs to three sentences or fewer.

task: Summarize in two sentences: the team agreed to move the release from Friday to Tuesday because the payment review is not finished, and Dana will tell the customers.
rubric: The new release day (Tuesday) and the old one (Friday) are both stated.
The unfinished payment review is given as the reason.
Dana is named as the person who informs the customers.
The summary is two sentences long.

task: Write a one-line summary of a change that adds a retry to the export job and fixes a typo in the help text.
rubric: The line mentions the retry added to the export job.
The line mentions the typo fix in the help text.
It fits on one line and reads as a single statement.

task: Explain in under 80 words why a cache can return stale data.
rubric: The answer states that a cache holds a copy that can differ from the source after the source changes.
It mentions at least one way staleness is limited, such as expiry times or invalidation.
It uses fewer than eighty words.

task: Suggest a name for a function that returns the number of days between two dates, and names for its two parameters.
rubric: The function name says that it counts days between dates.
The two parameter names tell the reader which date comes first and which comes second, or what each one means.
No parameter is a single letter or an unclear abbreviation.

task: A variable holds the list of users who have not confirmed their email address. Suggest a name for it and explain the choice in one sentence.
rubric: The name says it is a collection of users and that they are unconfirmed.
The name is not a single letter or a cryptic short form.
The explanation is one sentence.

task: Name a class that wraps a connection to a mail server and sends messages. Also name two of its methods.
rubric: The class name says that it sends mail or talks to a mail server.
Two method names are given, and each one says what it does.
The names avoid single letters and obscure abbreviations.

task: Write the error message shown when a user uploads a file of 14 MB and the limit is 10 MB.
rubric: The message says the upload was rejected because the file is too large.
It includes the actual size, 14 MB, and the limit, 10 MB.
It tells the user what to do next, such as choosing a smaller file.

task: Write the error message shown when a configuration file named app.toml cannot be found in /etc/app.
rubric: The message says that the configuration file was not found.
It includes the file name and the directory that was searched.
It suggests a next step, such as creating the file or setting a different path.

task: Write error messages for two cases: a password shorter than 12 characters, and a username that is already taken.
rubric: Two messages are given, one for each case.
The password message states the minimum of 12 characters.
The username message names the taken username or says clearly that it is taken.
Each message tells the user what to do next.
